top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) rest on a traceable record: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice and first strontium clock, then Ye's group taking systematics to 10^-18, reproduced independently at JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and NPL, and already used as a probe of constants and gravitational redshift. The principle is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and the two-name allocation matches the decisive contributions. Topological insulators (P002) are a deeper discovery but the three-name cut leaves unresolved credit (Mele, Hasan, Zhang) and a 2016 overlap; a no-award outcome is worse than either mature candidate.
